title: Already below the norm
hook: Could a conservation message make a low-use household consume more?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a descriptive average from an approval signal for already desirable behavior.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Distinguish a descriptive average from an approval signal for already desirable behavior.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy norm-following rule moves use halfway from forty toward sixty units. What use does it produce? Toy inputs A=[40, 60, 0.5]; B=[40, 60, 0].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[50, 40, 60], [40, 40, 60]]. Labels: Next units, Current units, Norm units.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: Moving toward an average can increase an already-low user’s consumption in this rule. The comparison preserves the low level instead. Descriptive information and an approval signal need not produce the same modeled response.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Current units=40, Norm units=60, Move fraction=0. What is Next units? Answer: 40.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Current units=40, Norm units=60, Move fraction=0. What is Next units?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 40. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Low energy users told they were below average increased use, unless the report added a smiley face of approval (Schultz et al., 2007).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Distinguish a descriptive average from an approval signal for already desirable behavior.
